as_written_in_papers.quote: Whole-exome sequencing revealed a novel compound heterozygous mutation in LPIN2: c.2349del (p.Glu784ArgfsTer8), inherited from the mother, and c.2327+3A>G, inherited from the father (Figure 3).

cases.statement: One affected person (a girl, compound heterozygous with c.2349del) and her father (carrier, no symptoms reported) in a single family, PMID 41113563.

people.label: patient (proband)
people.key_phenotypes: recurrent knee and ankle swelling and pain from 1 y 8 mo; low-grade fever with elevated CRP/ESR during attacks; mild microcytic anemia; multifocal bone marrow edema on MRI

quotes.quote: A 3-year and 10-month-old girl was admitted to our hospital on November 9, 2021, with a history of intermittent joint pain for more than two years, first manifesting at 1 year and 8 months of age.
Each attack was associated with low-grade fever and elevated inflammatory markers, including C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR).
During the attack phase, laboratory findings showed mild anemia (hemoglobin 103 g/L; reference 112–149 g/L), with microcytic indices (MCV 81.5 fL, MCH 26.2 pg).
Imaging of the lower limbs revealed bone marrow edema and soft tissue swelling involving both distal femurs (Figure 1), the proximal left tibia, and both ankles.

people.label: father of patient
people.zygosity_or_genotype: carrier (variant inherited from him); zygosity not stated in words, heterozygous implied
people.key_phenotypes: no symptoms reported; abnormal splicing band on RT-PCR; LPIN2 mRNA level within normal range

quotes.quote: Validation of splice site function: the father and the patient have abnormal cutting bands.
quantitative RT-PCR analysis revealed that the LPIN2 mRNA level in the proband's father was within the normal range
The child was the first pregnancy and first delivery (G1P1), and no family history of similar symptoms was reported.

phenotype_specificity.statement: CRMO-like multifocal bone marrow edema plus mild microcytic anemia; autoimmune and infectious workups were negative. No dyserythropoietic morphology is described in the marrow. The paper does not say whether other genes were excluded on whole-exome sequencing.

quotes.quote: Immunological markers, including ANA, HLA-B27, rheumatoid factor, and anti-CCP, were negative, and 25-hydroxyvitamin D was normal.
Extensive infectious workup was negative, including anti-streptolysin O, Epstein–Barr virus, respiratory pathogens, parvovirus B19, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae.
Bone marrow cytology showed 21% erythroid precursors (Figure 2), predominantly at the intermediate and late stages, with mild anisocytosis among mature erythrocytes.

segregation.statement: No other affected relatives; unaffected father carries the variant; unaffected mother carries the other allele; proband is an only child.

quotes.quote: The child was the first pregnancy and first delivery (G1P1), and no family history of similar symptoms was reported.

de_novo.statement: Not de novo: inherited from the father. Both parents were sequenced. Parentage confirmation is not reported.

quotes.quote: c.2349del (p.Glu784ArgfsTer8), a frameshift mutation inherited from the mother, and c.2327+3A>G, a splice-site mutation inherited from the father.

in_trans.statement: Other allele c.2349del from the mother; phase was shown by parental testing.

quotes.quote: Peripheral blood (2 ml) was collected from the patient and her parents for whole-exome sequencing, and candidate variants were confirmed by Sanger sequencing and interpreted using ACMG guidelines.
c.2349del (p.Glu784ArgfsTer8), a frameshift mutation inherited from the mother, and c.2327+3A>G, a splice-site mutation inherited from the father.

functional.statement: RT-PCR on patient-derived blood RNA (PAXgene), with gel electrophoresis and sequencing, showed abnormal bands in the father and the proband and exon 17 skipping. On qRT-PCR the father's LPIN2 mRNA level was within the normal range, so per the authors exon 17 skipping did not lower mRNA. The paper does not describe a normal control sample for the gel or give numbers. It does not say whether the exon 17 skip is in frame, or how much normally spliced transcript remains.

quotes.quote: In addition, RNA samples were collected in PAXgene tubes, reverse-transcribed into cDNA, and analyzed by gel electrophoresis and sequencing.
RNA analysis confirmed abnormal splicing with exon 17 skipping (Figure 4)
Validation of splice site function: the father and the patient have abnormal cutting bands.
quantitative results showed that the skipping in exon 17 caused by the abnormal splicing did not affect the mRNA level of the LPIN2 gene

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Intronic donor-region variant at +3 (protein effect p.?; from the batch HGVS). The authors report exon 17 skipping. They speculate that loss of exon 17 (C-LIP domain) disrupts catalytic function and nuclear localization, and that a splice-site allele may allow residual activity.

quotes.quote: exon 17 is located in the C-LIP structural domain, which may disrupt the enzyme's active center and affect its catalytic function
the protein produced by the deletion of this exon is likely unable to enter the nucleus properly to perform its regulatory function in the nucleus
A plausible explanation is that the compound heterozygous state, which includes a splice-site mutation, may permit some residual Lipin-2 activity (10), thereby attenuating disease severity.

computational_predictions.statement: VarSEAK predicted altered mRNA splicing (no score given).

quotes.quote: The first variant was classified as likely pathogenic, while the second was predicted by VarSEAK to alter mRNA splicing.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Not in HGMD, dbSNP or 1000 Genomes per the authors (gnomAD not mentioned).

quotes.quote: Neither variant was reported in HGMD, dbSNP, or the 1000 Genomes Project.

authors_classification.statement: No ACMG class stated for this variant. The abstract says the RNA analysis established the pathogenicity of the splice-site variant.

quotes.quote: RNA analysis confirmed exon 17 skipping, carried out quantitative RT-PCR analysis of LPIN2 mRNA,establishing pathogenicity of the splice-site variant.

concerns: No ACMG class is given for this variant, only 'establishing pathogenicity' in the abstract.
The paper does not state whether the exon 17 skip is in frame, how much normally spliced transcript remains, or what normal control was used in the RT-PCR gel.
The exon numbering (exon 17) is the authors'; the paper names no transcript.
Another variant at the same intron donor site, c.2327+1G>C, appears in the paper's review table of earlier patients (e.g. H1, I1, I2, K1). That is a different variant, given only as context.
Same person also carries candidate G-majeed-002 (c.2349del).

notes_for_panel: This is the only candidate in the batch with variant-specific RNA evidence: exon 17 skipping in carrier and proband blood RNA. The paper gives no control details or quantification of the skipped and full-length products.
